Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failing test `testToClass_object()` calls `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` with an array containing a null element. The test expects the result array to contain `null` at the corresponding position, but the current implementation throws a NullPointerException (NPE).

Inspecting the implementation of `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])`:
- It returns null if input is null.
- Returns an empty class array if input is empty.
- Otherwise, it creates a new `Class<?>[]` of the same length as the input array.
- It then loops through the input array and sets each element of the output array to the class of the corresponding input element by calling `array[i].getClass()`.
- This direct call to `array[i].getClass()` causes an NPE if `array[i]` is null because it tries to invoke a method on a null reference.

The current bug report `'c0.m0(Object[]) throws NPE on null array element'` directly matches this reasoning.

The expected behavior (according to the test) is that if an element in the input array is null, the corresponding output element should be null rather than causing an exception.

Therefore, the root cause is that `toClass(Object[])` does not handle null elements appropriately in its loop. The method should check if `array[i]` is null and, if so, assign null to `classes[i]` instead of calling `getClass()`.

No other recent bug reports directly relate to this problem.

This diagnosis explains why the test fails with an NPE and what the fix should involve.
